title: plan-tasks
description:
Per-row schema for the plan `## Tasks` task-spine YAML block (one task object per row). Full authoring contract, parser-locate rule, malformed-row disposition, and harvest routing: docs/wiki/writing-plans.md § Machine-Parseable Task Spine and docs/wiki/canonical-artifact-shapes.md § Addressable-Section Convention.

Spec backlink: pln-full-coverage-planning-posture-bca96f § C1 (pinned task-spine contract).

id.description: Chunk id (e.g. C1, D1). Unique within the plan. Deferred rows conventionally use the D<n> prefix, but the prefix is a convention, not a schema-enforced discriminator — `deferred: true` is the actual signal.

title.description: One-line brief. Becomes the queue-entry title on harvest (coordinator-queue-append --schema improvement-queue, or the lessons-outbox title on the doctrine-edit/snippet-sync-update path).

change_kind.description: WIDER UNIVERSAL change-kind enum. SSOT: docs/wiki/lessons-outbox-schema.md § Change-kind enum (do NOT duplicate the enum values elsewhere — point there instead). Harvest routing: the project-tier subset (script-edit, skill-edit, wiki-append, wiki-new, hook-edit, agent-prompt-edit, doc-edit, test-edit, code-edit, config-edit, verification) routes to coordinator-queue-append --schema improvement-queue; doctrine-edit and snippet-sync-update route to coordinator-lesson-promote (lessons-outbox) instead — the improvement-queue schema rejects those two kinds at project scope. These values name the SURFACE changed, not the flavour of the change — do not coin a work-shape token (a bash-to-Python port of a bin/ utility is script-edit); an unrecognized value routes nowhere on harvest. MIGRATION NOTE, no legacy values retained: this enum is CLOSED to the `-edit`-suffixed set plus `verification` deliberately, mirroring the closed-enum, no-coined-token discipline this field's SSOT already enforces (docs/wiki/lessons-outbox-schema.md § Change-kind enum, "A work-shape word is not an enum member") — reopening it to admit a retired pre-migration token would reintroduce the exact drift that section forbids. `change_kind` is NOT in the corpus-gate's registered schema map (`coordinator/tests/test_artifact_corpus_validates_against_schema.py :: _CORPUS_SCHEMA_MAP` carries no plan-tasks entry), so a pre-migration row authored under an earlier vocabulary is not retroactively re-validated by this schema and is not broken in place; only newly-authored/re-validated rows must use the current closed set. A caller that DOES whole-row-validate an existing plan's task spine against this schema version (e.g. a linter run over an old plan) should treat a `change_kind` outside the current enum as a stale-authoring-vocabulary finding to re-tag at the row, not a corpus-wide migration to script.

surface.description: Harvest/coverage PRIMARY-TARGET field — a single path or subsystem. Maps to the queue entry's `surface` field ONLY. See docs/wiki/writing-plans.md § Machine-Parseable Task Spine for the surface-vs-write-files-set distinction.

queue_scope.description: Which improvement-queue the harvest writes into. Default 'project' writes to the plan's own repo-local state/improvement-queue/. 'central' is a per-deferral opt-in that maps to `coordinator-queue-append --queue-scope central`.

execution_mode.description: WHO can execute this row. 'agent' (default) => an ordinary dispatchable row. 'operator' => the work is runnable ONLY by a human at an interactive terminal, so the row is excluded from dispatch and surfaced to a human instead (`coordinator_core/ops/dispatch_emit/spine_read.py :: _is_operator_row`, on the same non-dispatchable path an uncleared `external_gate` takes). It is an execution-capability claim, NOT a resolution state: an `operator` row stays `disposition: open`, keeps its `writes`, and is still counted by close-out. NEGATIVE SPEC, three exclusions, each a route that was tried and is a false statement on the spine: (1) `external_gate` requires `owner_repo`, which names another REPO — the blocking party here is the operator, and a fabricated owner_repo also fails the whole emission on Check A, taking unrelated chunks down with it. (2) `deferred: true` asserts a scope cut and pulls in `pm_approved`/`case_against` — the row is not deferred, it is next. (3) a closed `disposition` is a stealth-skip: the work has not happened. The enum is closed at two members; a third naming WHICH human or WHICH terminal is a routing claim the dispatcher cannot act on, and belongs in `body`.

deferred.description: true => this row is NOT shipped by this plan; it is a harvest candidate for coordinator-harvest-deferrals. false (default) => the row is shipped in-plan and is not a harvest target.

pm_approved.description: Required when deferred is true (cross-field rule — see the allOf conditional below). Records that the PM ratified the scope cut. false or absent on a deferred:true row is a plan-coverage-checker flag. Only deferred:true AND pm_approved:true rows are harvest candidates; a deferred row with pm_approved:false or absent is NOT harvested. READ-TOLERATED, not authoritative, on any plan carrying a plan-document-level `grouping_approvals` block (a GOVERNED plan — see plan.schema.json, where that field is defined): on a governed plan this bare bool is NOT the authorization signal for a closed row: authorization lives in the plan-document `grouping_approvals` block, keyed by the grouping (`do`/`defer`/`ruled_out`) the row's `disposition` derives into (see schema_validate.py's `check_plan_tasks_grouping_approval`). On a LEGACY plan (no such block present anywhere in its frontmatter), this field is unchanged from its original role — the sole authorization signal for a deferred/closed row, read-tolerated exactly as before this distinction existed.

body.description: Optional multi-line detail block. Maps to the queue entry's `body` field on harvest.

disposition.description: Row resolution state. 'open' (default) => not yet resolved. 'coded' => shipped in a specific commit (disposition_ref is a single hex SHA). 'spun_off' => moved to a new plan (disposition_ref is a single repo-relative path). 'backlogged' => deferred to the improvement/debt backlog (disposition_ref is a single repo-relative path). 'wont_do' => explicitly declined (disposition_ref forbidden; disposition_detail required). NEGATIVE SPEC: 'landed' and 'done' are NOT values here and never become ones -- both are words writers reach for meaning 'shipped', which is spelled 'coded'. The enum is closed; an out-of-enum value is admitted by the write path today and then read differently by different consumers, one refusing outright and one defaulting it to 'open', so a shipped row silently reads as unstarted. Widening this enum would make that divergence permanent rather than fixing it. Mirrors the shape of `carried_items[].disposition` (D1). Cross-field enforcement matrix: D2/D3/D4 in the originating plan; hard rejection happens in schema_validate.py (C2), not here — see the allOf $comments below for what this schema itself does and does not hard-fail.

disposition_ref.description: Forward pointer/evidence for a non-open disposition — semantics depend on `disposition` (SHA for coded, repo-relative path for spun_off/backlogged, forbidden for wont_do). Separate from `disposition_detail`, which carries rationale prose (D2).

depends_on.description: OPTIONAL declared sequencing edges into this row, one entry per predecessor. ABSENT (or empty) means no non-write-overlap gate — it does NOT mean the row is unconditionally parallel, because write-overlap gates are computed elsewhere and are never written here. Exists so the two gate kinds that are NOT derivable from the file-write graph have a home on the spine instead of living only in wave-map prose the EM must re-derive at execute time. Authoring procedure: docs/wiki/writing-plans.md § Substrate-Migration Sequencing step 2. Gate-kind semantics and the malformed-serialization rule: skills/execute-plan/SKILL.md Phase 1.6 § gate-kind discriminator. NEGATIVE SPEC — three of the six discriminator gate kinds are deliberately unwritable here, see `gate_kind`'s enum note.

chunk.description: The predecessor row's `id` (e.g. C1, D2) within THIS plan's spine. Singular referent — one predecessor per entry; a row with three predecessors carries three entries, which is why this field is an array member rather than the singular `depends_on: <Task K>` scalar the wiki originally prescribed.

gate_kind.description: Which Phase 1.6 gate this edge is. DELIBERATELY RESTRICTED to the two gate kinds that a mechanical wave-builder cannot derive on its own. `output-consumption-runtime`: the predecessor's artifact must EXIST AT RUNTIME when this row executes (the layout/substrate case — a directory, schema, or persistence path the producer opens). `epistemic-premise`: the predecessor decides whether this row should exist at all, so there is no interface to pin and nothing to author against until its verdict lands. NEGATIVE SPEC, three exclusions, each for its own reason: (1) `file-write-overlap` is COMPUTED by the wave-builder from the chunks' write targets (skills/execute-plan/SKILL.md:128) and must NEVER be hand-declared here — a hand-written write-overlap edge is a second, silently-desyncing source of truth for a fact the graph already knows. (2) `output-consumption-content` and (3) `contract-change` do not gate AUTHORING at all: Phase 1.6 requires both to downgrade to concurrent-with-pinned-interface with verification deferred to merge, so declaring either as a dependency edge is precisely the malformed serialization the discriminator exists to catch — pin the interface in the consumer's body instead. `none` is likewise unwritable: absence of the field is how a row says it has no declared gate.

note.description: OPTIONAL one-line rationale for the edge — what specifically must exist (or be decided) before this row runs. Reader-facing prose; no consumer parses it. Cheap and worth writing: the edge's KIND is machine-readable via `gate_kind`, but the reason a human should trust the edge is not.

disposition_detail.description: Rationale/detail prose for a CLOSED disposition (spun_off/backlogged/wont_do — D2/D4). Required for wont_do (in place of disposition_ref) and for spun_off/backlogged alongside their disposition_ref. NOT required for coded: per D3, coded is evidence of work done, not a scope decision, so it carries no PM rationale to record — see the allOf conditionals below for the exact per-disposition requirement.

case_against.description: The strongest HONEST case for doing this work now, plus the EM's recommendation, confidence, and what would change it. Required when disposition is backlogged or wont_do (D4-adjacent, mirroring pm_approved's trigger set — see the allOf conditional below); deliberately NOT required for spun_off (nothing leaves the corpus, so there is no scope cut to argue against — see the pm_approved conditional's own $comment for the ruling this mirrors). Presence-only / NON-hard-failing at this schema layer, exactly like the sibling conditionals: this only checks that the key exists on the row, not that its prose is non-vacuous. A strawman satisfies this schema while defeating the rule it exists to serve — the field asks for the strongest honest case, not a token counter-argument to grep past.

items.description: A concrete file path. A trailing separator is refused: a directory is not a committable path, and stripping the separator strands the wave. A row whose filenames are chosen at run time declares the directory under `writes_under` instead.

writes.description: Repo-relative paths (plain strings; no glob syntax in this version) this task writes. Optional — absence means 'undeclared', not 'writes nothing'. Feeds write-overlap/wave-map derivation as a pure function of the spine.

writes_under.description: Directory prefixes, each ending in `/` or `\`, for a row whose output filenames are chosen at run time. Joins write-overlap and read-after-write ordering like `writes`. The executor names the files it wrote under each prefix, and the commit takes exactly those, bounded to this row's prefixes. A row declaring a prefix and omitting `writes` reads as `writes: []`, never undeclared. A single known file belongs in `writes`. A memo row needs neither: `memo.send` commits in the receiver's tree, so it spells `writes: []`.

reads.description: Repo-relative paths this task reads without writing. Optional. Same string-array shape as writes:. Participates in wave ordering alongside writes: — the wave-builder computes the write-overlap gate from both writes:/reads:, so a row's reads: is not merely informational.

external_gate.description: OPTIONAL declared blockers on work owned by ANOTHER repo — a sibling field to depends_on, not nested in it, because an external blocker has no local predecessor row to reference (depends_on[].chunk resolves only within THIS plan's spine). One entry per blocking party — a row blocked on two repos carries two entries. Authoring procedure: docs/wiki/writing-plans.md § Machine-Parseable Task Spine. NEGATIVE SPEC: this is NOT for intra-plan edges — a predecessor that is a row in THIS plan's spine belongs on depends_on, never here, regardless of wording. It is also NOT a substitute for the write-overlap gate the wave-builder computes from writes:/reads: — never hand-declare a same-repo write conflict here.

owner_repo.description: The repo that owns the blocking work, as its bare hyphenated shortname (e.g. Claude-klabauter, claude-klabauter) — confirm the spelling with `machine-local keys | grep '^repos\.'` first; a wrong guess returns a bare not-found that reads as 'no such repo,' not as a hint to try another key. NEGATIVE SPEC: never this repo's own shortname — an intra-repo blocker belongs on `depends_on`, not here — and never a session id.

condition.description: What must become true in owner_repo before this row executes (or, if blocks is ac-closure, before the gated criterion can close). Reader-facing prose, not a machine-evaluated predicate — no consumer parses this for truth, only a human deciding whether the gate has cleared.

closure_evidence.description: OPTIONAL — how closure is verified: a memo path, a commit SHA, a probe command. Absence means the author has not yet named how they'll recognize closure, not that the gate never clears. Distinct from `cleared`: this names how closure was or will be verified, not that it already has been — an author naming a probe they have not yet run sets this WITHOUT `cleared`.

cleared.description: OPTIONAL — asserts the gate IS discharged, as distinct from `closure_evidence` naming how that was or will be verified. `cleared: true` clears the gate outright. `cleared: false` is an explicit negative that overrides a truthy `closure_evidence` — it does not clear the gate even when evidence is named.

closure_key.description: OPTIONAL — the machine-matchable IDENTITY of the thing whose landing discharges this gate, as distinct from `condition` (reader-facing prose, never machine-evaluated) and `closure_evidence` (how closure was or will be verified). A reader matches this against the `discharges.closure_key` block on a cross-repo memo delivered by owner_repo, and on a match may PROPOSE the `cleared: true` flip with a citation — it never performs it. `cleared: true` remains the one clearing path; nothing here clears a gate. Writable BEFORE the discharge by construction: a key naming something that cannot exist until after the work lands is evidence, not a gate declaration, and belongs on `closure_evidence`.

kind.description: Which identity namespace `id` is drawn from. `deliverable`: a `dlv-<slug>-<6hex>` deliverable_id (plan.schema.json's `deliverable_id`) — the fleet's durable, path-independent join key, minted once at the earliest artifact and carried verbatim downstream by plan, handoff, completion-entry, goal, and the Deliverable-Id commit trailer. `memo-thread`: a memo basename, in the same form `in_reply_to` normalizes to (bare basename, matched case-insensitively with or without the `.md`) — the identity for a gate that blocks on owner_repo actioning a named ask. NEGATIVE SPEC, four exclusions, each for its own reason: (1) `commit` is unwritable here — a SHA does not exist at authoring time, and a SHA naming work already done is `closure_evidence`, which would give one fact two desyncing homes. (2) `schema-version` (`<schema>@<x-schema-version>`) is deliberately excluded even though contract-bump gates are common: its value is that the WAITING repo evaluates it locally against its own vendored copy, making it a predicate rather than a join key against an emitted record — mixing the two forces every reader to branch on `kind` to know whether to look outward or inward. A future `closure_probe` field is the right home if a census earns one. (3) `plan-path`/`plan_id` are excluded because path-shaped ids rename silently and a plan's existence is not its discharge; `deliverable` is the rename-proof identity for the same intent. (4) `commitment` (a state/cross-repo-commitments/ record) is excluded because that ledger is receiver-side-only and repo-local by explicit negative spec — the owner repo, the one discharging, cannot write or reference it.

id.description: The identity value, in the namespace `kind` names. Interpreted within owner_repo — ids are minted per-repo with no repo qualifier, so `owner_repo` supplies the namespace and a bare id is never globally resolvable on its own.

requires.description: OPTIONAL for schema validity, REQUIRED by the mise-prep authoring bar on any UNCLEARED entry. What would clear this gate, DECLARED rather than read off `condition`. `landed-work`: owner_repo lands work that already exists as their plan — an ordinary blocked row, withheld by the wave-builder at ROW granularity, and the plan around it still certifies. `commit-in-owner-repo`: DISQUALIFYING — clearing it needs a commit INTO owner_repo's tree, which needs per-session PM assent obtained at execution dispatch (DR-127), so the whole plan is refused for `mise-prepped`. NEGATIVE SPEC: this is not a severity and not a restatement of `blocks` — `blocks` says WHAT the gate holds up, `requires` says WHAT WOULD CLEAR IT, and both are read. It is not derivable from `condition`, which that field's own description states no consumer parses for truth. An entry with `cleared: true` is not read here — a discharged gate has nothing left to require. Checked by coordinator/bin/mise-prep-gate.py; authoring bar: coordinator/docs/wiki/mise-prepped-authoring-bar.md § External dependencies.

blocks.description: OPTIONAL, defaults to execution. `execution`: this row cannot run until the gate clears — the wave-builder must not schedule it. `ac-closure`: the row executes normally; only the gated criterion's closure is blocked — the plan's prime exit criterion (docs/wiki/writing-plans.md), not a cell in the now-collapsed AC checkbox table; the table is gone, but a gate that holds up closure without blocking execution is still a distinct thing this value names and nothing else does. This distinction is load-bearing — conflating the two stalls an executable chunk on a gate that only blocks its criterion's closure, not its execution. Any future removal of this value (should the concept itself ever genuinely die) is joint DoE+engine work tracked on claude-klabauter's re-vendor of this schema, not folded into any plan narrowing depends_on/gate-kind clearing semantics — that is a different, unrelated hazard.

agent_type.description:
WHICH agent runs this row, overriding the write-target derivation entirely. Optional; absent, the emitter derives the type from `writes` as it always has (any `docs/plans/*.md` or `docs/problems/*.md` path routes to `coordinator:enricher`, everything else to `coordinator:executor`), so a spine that omits this key emits exactly as before. Optionally plugin-qualified: `coordinator:workflow-maker`, `Explore`. A malformed value fails LOUD at emit, never at runtime, matching the posture of `MixedAgentTypeRowError`; a well-formed value naming an agent the engine does not know is passed through rather than refused -- the engine does not own this repo's agent roster, and inventing a validation it cannot honestly perform would be worse than the pass-through. REQUIRES `agent_model` WHENEVER the engine carries no model row for the named agent: `_model_opt` refuses an explicit `agent_type` with no `_AGENT_MODELS` entry unless `agent_model` accompanies it, and names `agent_model` as the fix. So for any agent the engine does not already model, the pair is mandatory, not optional.

NEGATIVE SPEC -- this is not the fan-out escape hatch. A chunk whose work is dispatching N sub-agents is N chunks (one worker per row, disjoint `writes`, all depending on the row producing their shared input), NOT one row naming a dispatch-capable agent. Decomposition makes independence a property of the spine rather than something an executor arranges at runtime, and it needs no agent field at all. Reach for `agent_type` only where decomposition does not dissolve the need. See `docs/wiki/coordinator-tripwires/a-chunk-that-wants-to-dispatch-n-workers-is-n-chunks.md`.

The mixed-row refusal is NOT overridden by this field, and that ordering is deliberate: a row whose `writes` span both an immutable plan/problem body and ordinary code is incoherent whoever runs it, so naming an agent does not reconcile the two halves -- the spine still needs splitting.

agent_model.description:
WHICH model the row's agent runs on. Optional ONLY when the engine already carries a model row for the row's agent; required alongside any `agent_type` it does not (the emit refuses and names this field). Absent on a row with no `agent_type`, model selection is unchanged.

WHY THIS EXISTS, and why it is not a nicety beside `agent_type`: the emitter resolves a model by table lookup with a silent default (`_AGENT_MODELS.get(agent_type, 'sonnet')`). An agent type absent from that table therefore emits a Sonnet dispatch with nothing raised and nothing logged. So `agent_type` alone would be a knob whose failure mode is naming an Opus persona and quietly getting Sonnet -- and the first consumer (`coordinator:workflow-maker`) is itself Sonnet, so the hole would have shipped looking correct. The two fields land together; do not treat this one as optional scaffolding to add later.

allOf.$comment: Cross-field rule: pm_approved is required-when-deferred. JSON Schema if/then encodes this — when deferred is true, pm_approved MUST be present (and, per the field's semantics, true) for the row to be a valid harvest candidate. A deferred:true row with pm_approved absent or false remains structurally valid JSON (this schema does not hard-fail it — see the malformed-row-disposition note in the top-level description) but is flagged by plan-coverage-checker, the enforcement surface for this cross-field rule.

then.$comment: Presence, not truthiness — this only checks that pm_approved is a key on the row. A deferred:true row with pm_approved:false still validates here (schema does not hard-fail it); the truthiness check (pm_approved must equal literal true) is flagged by plan-coverage-checker, not schema-rejected.

allOf.$comment: Cross-field rule: disposition: coded requires disposition_ref matching a single hex SHA (7-40 hex chars) — DR-096's singular-referent constraint (D2): no ranges, comma-lists, or branch names.
Cross-field rule: disposition: spun_off requires disposition_ref as a single repo-relative path (DR-096 singular-referent — one path, not a list).
Cross-field rule: disposition: backlogged requires disposition_ref as a single repo-relative path (DR-096 singular-referent — one path, not a list).
Cross-field rule: disposition: wont_do requires disposition_detail and FORBIDS disposition_ref (there is no forward pointer for a declined row).

Cross-field rule: the two SCOPE-CUT dispositions (backlogged/wont_do) require pm_approved (D4, as narrowed by DR-2026-08-05 below). `coded` is deliberately NOT gated: per D3 it is evidence of work done, not a scope decision, so it needs no PM authorization. `spun_off`'s gate is the `spun_off` grouping in plan.schema.json's `grouping_approvals`, checked by `check_plan_tasks_grouping_approval` — not this branch. That gate is DECLARABLE but NOT YET LIVE: the predicate does not scan `spun_off` until claude-klabauter re-vendors plan.schema.json and widens its GOVERNED-leg set, so today a `spun_off` row closes ungated on governed and legacy plans alike. It is deliberately absent from this trigger set because this branch is legacy-only (see LEGACY-ONLY BRANCH below) and every plan carrying a spun_off row predates the grouping contract: widening here would retroactively invalidate rows authored correctly under the rules then in force, and the only way to revalidate them is to write `pm_approved: true` onto rows no PM ever approved — forging assent in the exact field the gate exists to make meaningful. A plan enters the contract by ACQUIRING the grouping_approvals block; that acquisition is the migration event, and from it spun_off is gated like backlogged and wont_do. backlogged and wont_do DO drop work, and choosing between them is a PM judgment the EM does not self-issue; claude-klabauter-em's ask to relax them to a recorded-reason gate was declined (see cross-repo/outbox for the reply). Do not widen this enum to include spun_off — that is the governed layer's job, not this one — and do not narrow it further, without a PM ruling. Presence-only / NON-hard-failing at this schema layer, exactly like the deferred=>pm_approved rule's own $comment above: this only checks that pm_approved is a key on the row, not that it equals literal true. Hard rejection of `pm_approved is not True` on a closed disposition is schema_validate.py's job (C2's _cf_plan_tasks_disposition_shape — the plan-tasks-specific caller, not the shared _cf_disposition_shape), not this file's. LEGACY-ONLY BRANCH: on a GOVERNED plan (one whose frontmatter carries a plan-document-level `grouping_approvals` block — see plan.schema.json), claude-klabauter's frontmatter layer derives a governed schema variant at validation time (`schema_validate.py`'s `_plan_tasks_schema_without_pm_approved_required`) that STRIPS this exact branch — any `allOf` branch whose `then.required` names `pm_approved` is removed from the derived copy — because a governed plan's closed-row authorization is instead checked against the row's grouping approval state (`check_plan_tasks_grouping_approval`), not this per-row bool. This branch therefore governs LEGACY plans only; do not hand-copy a second, governed-only variant of it into this file. The derivation is computed once, at runtime, from this single branch — a hand-maintained duplicate here would be a second home for the same rule, free to silently desync from the branch it duplicates.

Cross-field rule: the two SCOPE-CUT dispositions (backlogged/wont_do) also require case_against — the both-sides ask (cross-repo/inbox/2026-08-06-claude-klabauter-em-deferrals-need-both-sides-not-a-ratify-list.md; docs/plans/2026-08-06-deferrals-carry-both-sides.md). Shares the pm_approved conditional's trigger set immediately above, but for its OWN reason, not by parity: `case_against` is the argument against DROPPING work, and a spun-off row drops none — the work continues in a named successor. Approving a move and arguing against a drop are different asks, so widening this trigger to spun_off would make case_against a box-tick on the one closed disposition where it has no content. `spun_off` IS PM-gated, at the grouping layer (plan.schema.json's `grouping_approvals.spun_off`); its assent and its argument are deliberately scoped differently, so do not re-derive this trigger set from that one. Presence-only / NON-hard-failing at this schema layer, exactly like every other conditional in this file: this checks that case_against is a key on the row, not that its prose is non-vacuous. Hard rejection is claude-klabauter-resident and landed (`eee18fb77`) as absent/empty/whitespace-only refusal — presence and non-blankness only. Anti-strawman detection was deliberately NOT built: a case against phrased weakly enough to lose satisfies any mechanical check, so that is a doctrine and review-gate problem (docs/wiki/plan-coverage-checker.md Lens 2b specificity sub-check), not a validator's. NOT-SUPPRESSED-ON-GOVERNED: the mirroring stops at the trigger set. Claude-klabauter's governed-plan schema variant (`_plan_tasks_schema_without_pm_approved_required`) strips only allOf branches whose `then.required` names `pm_approved`; this branch requires `case_against`, so it survives, and claude-klabauter's own gate fires regardless of governed=True. That is correct and deliberate on both sides — `case_against` is the argument FOR the cut, not the authorization OF it, so it is orthogonal to the governance model.

Cross-field rule: the CLOSED dispositions other than wont_do (spun_off/backlogged) also require disposition_detail — rationale prose alongside the evidence pointer (D2/D4: 'the verbatim PM reasoning ... goes in disposition_detail — which is already required on every CLOSED disposition'). wont_do's disposition_detail requirement is already covered by its own conditional above. `coded` is deliberately excluded here: per D3 it is evidence of work done, not a scope decision, and is therefore NOT a CLOSED disposition — close_out_and_stamp's auto-resolution to coded writes only disposition + disposition_ref (the commit SHA) and must remain schema-valid with no detail.
